points: A famine in Canaan sent Elimelech, Naomi and their two sons from Bethlehem-judah to the country of Moab, the same way a famine sent Jacob's family to Egypt.
Elimelech died, the sons took Moabite wives, Orpah and Ruth, and then the sons died too, leaving Naomi with no man in the house.

note.label: The Nativity: the Bloodline, Birthright, & the Messiah

points: There was a famine in the land, and Elimelech of Bethlehemjudah went to sojourn in the country of Moab with his wife Naomi and his two sons Mahlon and Chilion, Ephrathites of Bethlehemjudah.

note.label: Ruth 1: Naomi and Ruth Return from Moab

points: The daughters in law said, Surely we will return with thee unto thy people; but Naomi answered, Are there yet any more sons in my womb, that they may be your husbands? Even if she had a husband that night and bore sons, would they tarry until the boys were grown? They were grown women; they were not going to wait.

Naomi was free of her responsibility toward them: her husband had died, her sons their husbands had died, and their husbands had left them inheritances in Moab. She would not put them under an oath to stay and wait for sons that would likely never come.

note.label: Ruth 1: Naomi and Ruth Return from Moab

points: When Naomi saw that Ruth was stedfastly minded to go with her, she left speaking unto her, and the two went until they came to Bethlehem, where all the city was moved about them and said, Is this Naomi?

note.label: Ruth 1: Naomi and Ruth Return from Moab

points: She answered, Call me not Naomi, call me Mara: for the Almighty hath dealt very bitterly with me. I went out full, and the Lord hath brought me home again empty.

note.label: Ruth 1: Naomi and Ruth Return from Moab

points: So Naomi returned, and Ruth the Moabitess her daughter in law with her, and they came to Bethlehem in the beginning of barley harvest.

note.label: Ruth 1: Naomi and Ruth Return from Moab

points: Naomi had a kinsman of her husband, a mighty man of wealth of the family of Elimelech, and his name was Boaz.

note.label: Ruth 2: Gleaning in the Field of Boaz

points: Ruth asked Naomi, Let me now go to the field and glean ears of corn after him in whose sight I shall find grace; and her hap was to light on a part of the field belonging unto Boaz, who was of the kindred of Elimelech.

note.label: Ruth 2: Gleaning in the Field of Boaz

points: Boaz came from Bethlehem and greeted his reapers, The Lord be with you; and they answered him, The Lord bless thee. When he asked whose damsel this was, the servant set over the reapers answered, It is the Moabitish damsel that came back with Naomi, and reported how she had asked to glean and had continued from the morning with only a little rest in the house.

note.label: Ruth 2: Gleaning in the Field of Boaz

points: Naomi blessed him of the Lord, who hath not left off his kindness to the living and to the dead, and said, The man is near of kin unto us, one of our next kinsmen.

note.label: Ruth 2: Gleaning in the Field of Boaz

points: Naomi said, My daughter, shall I not seek rest for thee, that it may be well with thee? This is the same rest spoken of in chapter 1, rest in the house of a husband; and Boaz of their kindred was winnowing barley that night in the threshingfloor.

note.label: Ruth 3: The Skirt of the Near Kinsman

points: Boaz laid the matter before the kinsman: Naomi, that is come again out of the country of Moab, selleth a parcel of land which was our brother Elimelech's. If thou wilt redeem it, redeem it; but if not, tell me, for there is none to redeem it beside thee, and I am after thee. And the kinsman said, I will redeem it.

What day thou buyest the field of the hand of Naomi, thou must buy it also of Ruth the Moabitess, the wife of the dead, to raise up the name of the dead upon his inheritance. Whoever took the land had to take the dead brother's wife with it; Ruth the Moabitess came along as a parcel of the land, to keep the name of Mahlon alive.

Why did Naomi take that child from Ruth the Moabitess? Because it is not the custom of Israel to allow a child to be raised up under the hand of a heathen. Although Ruth was used to keep Mahlon's name alive in Israel, and although she was brought in, she was a vessel; she did not have the same standing of rights as an Israelite woman, and she had no hand in raising the child. Naomi took it and raised it as her own, so that it could learn the ways of Israel.
The neighbors said a son is born to Naomi, because the seed was raised up in the name of her dead husband and sons; that is why Obed is called hers.

note.label: The Nativity: the Bloodline, Birthright, & the Messiah

points: Naomi took the child, and laid it in her bosom, and became nurse unto it; and the women her neighbours gave it a name, saying, There is a son born to Naomi; and they called his name Obed: he is the father of Jesse, the father of David.

A child's first teacher is the mother: she is the one who nurses him, he spends all his time with her, and he takes on her ways. So what Naomi did in the spirit, she did immediately after that child was born: she took it and raised it as her own. Notice the neighbours said, There is a son born to Naomi; Naomi did not bear that son, Ruth did, but she took it as her own.
